source: J. Yao, S. Li, P. Zhang, S. Deng, G. Zhou, 'Dynamic Response and Damage Characteristics of Large Reinforced Concrete Slabs under Explosion', Applied Sciences 13 (2023) 12552, doi:10.3390/app132312552

slab.reinforcement: two mats, 10 mm HRB400 bars at 85 mm both ways; section ratio 1.2%
slab.cover_mm: 30 (Y) and 20 (X, Z), as the paper's simulation gives them
slab.supports: simply supported on the two long (5 m) sides on L-shaped RC supports, 150 mm bearing; the supports' height is not given

measured.note: T1-T3 pressures and displacements read by eye off Figures 6b and 7b (about +/-0.03 mm and +/-0.1 MPa); accelerations from Table 4; T4 from Section 3.3 and Figure 11.

T4.remarks: elliptical crater (the charge was two 10 kg cylinders); top bars exposed, not obviously broken; underside spalled over a medium range, bars exposed, bent and unbroken; over 10 long cracks on the underside; bent along the centre line; moderate damage
